correctness.rationale: Writing N=mk+r, each pair (y,z) is uniquely in row t≥0 with y+(b+1)z=r+tm. Divide r+tm by b+1 to get quotient h_t and remainder s_t. With j=h_t−z in [0,h_t], the threshold k for a nonnegative x is t+h_t+s_t+bj. Distinct (t,j) count separately, including ties. Since m=b(b+1)+1, row minima rise by b+2 without carry and by 2 with carry. Thus beyond the cheapest pair at (t,j)=(0,0), the next threshold is the minimum of row one's first threshold and, if q≥1, row zero's second threshold. This gives q+b+2 for s=b (including the tie when b=2,q≥1), s+b+2 for q=0,s<b and q+s+b otherwise, including q=b,s=0. Upon adding m, incrementing x retains all representations. Thus n_1 is the sum of the heights, and g_1 is max W_r−m. The four maxima of W_r are (2b+2)m−2, (3b−1)m−3, (2b+1)m+b−1 and (2b+1)m−1 for s=b, interior q≥1 and s<b, q=0 and s<b, and the endpoint q=b,s=0 respectively. Only the first two compete; their difference in the order second minus first is (b−3)m−1. Summing the three branches over q=0 and s<b, 1≤q≤b−1 and s<b, s=b, and the endpoint gives b(4b²+b+11)/2, counting zero as deficient. An independent x=0 pair-threshold enumeration corroborates all 3097 thresholds and both invariants for bases 2–20: python3 /workspace/branches/independent_replay.py 3. The row argument proves the unbounded b claim.

Subwattanachai's theorem needs an outside coin divisible by one of the other coins reduced by their pairwise gcd, and treats specified multiplicity levels. Here the pairwise gcds are 1,1,gcd(2,b). When the gcd is 1 no coin divides another (all three lie in [m,2m)); for gcd 2, twice m is greater than either remaining coin but less than twice either, so neither divides twice m.

value.rationale: The three minimal generators arise from a named family already studied at the ordinary Apéry layer. This complete second layer resolves all deficient residues at once, and the controlling maximum actually changes at b=4 rather than following the smallest cases. The explicit layer, transition and uniform count give useful exact information for comparisons with higher representation levels; the advancement is not the shared b=3 datum or the existence of a counting algorithm.
